title: Relative adjoint representation of a smooth group without an affineness hypothesis
statement:
Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian ring and $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $p:G\to S$ be a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] separated group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with identity $e:S\to G$. A group scheme here has multiplication, inverse and identity over $S$ satisfying the group diagrams; separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion. Define $\omega=e^*\Omega^1_{G/S}$ using relative differentials [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] and module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], and put $E=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_S}(\omega,\mathcal O_S)$. Then $E$ is a finite projective $A$-module, meaning a direct summand of $A^n$ for some finite $n$. The functor $R\mapsto\operatorname{Aut}_R(E\otimes_A R)$ on commutative $A$-algebras is represented by a smooth separated affine $S$-group scheme $\operatorname{GL}_S(E)$ of finite presentation. Affine has the meaning of [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Differentiation of conjugation defines an $S$-group homomorphism $\operatorname{Ad}_G:G\to\operatorname{GL}_S(E)$, and this morphism is of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For every commutative $A$-algebra $R$ there is a canonical $R$-linear identification
$$E\otimes_A R\cong\ker\bigl(G(R[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))\to G(R)\bigr),$$
where addition on the right is the group law and scalar multiplication is induced by $\epsilon\mapsto a\epsilon$. Under this identification $\operatorname{Ad}_G(g)$ sends a tangent point $v$ to $gvg^{-1}$, with $g\in G(R)$ viewed over the dual numbers by the constant inclusion. Formation of this tangent module, the representing general linear group, and the adjoint homomorphism commutes with arbitrary base change $A\to R$, compatibly with successive base changes. For every base change $A\to R$, the group $G_R$ is again smooth, separated and of finite presentation over $R$. In particular, for every map $A\to k$ to an algebraically closed field, $(\operatorname{Ad}_G)_k$ is the usual adjoint representation of $G_k$ on $T_eG_k$. No affineness or reductivity of $G$ is assumed, and $E=0$ is allowed.

source.place: Relative version of the adjoint action used in the first sentence of the proof of Proposition 6.3.16, printed p.229; background on Lie functors, p.2. Supporting local inputs read in literature/stacks-project: Tag 02G1 (morphisms-lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free) and Tag 022W (groupoids-example-general-linear-group). The arbitrary finite-projective tangent module and base-change formulation is agent-supplied. Conrad PDF read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf.

proof.text: By lem-ag-smooth-relative-differentials-finite-locally-free, $\Omega^1_{G/S}$ is finite locally free, with varying ranks allowed. Pulling back a local frame along $e$ gives local frames of $\omega$ by the tensor formula in def-pc-module-pullback. Thus $\omega$ is locally finitely presented and quasi-coherent by lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine. Put $W=\Gamma(S,\omega)$. Refine the frame cover to principal opens by lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open and take a finite subcover by lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact. The corresponding elements $f_i$ generate the unit ideal. The affine sections pullback formula identifies $W_{f_i}$ with the finite free sections of $\omega|_{D(f_i)}$. Lem-sc-affine-standard-cover-finite-projective now makes $W$ finite projective. Its dual is $E$: a sheaf map $\omega\to\mathcal O_S$ is determined on these local frames by its global-section map, and an $A$-linear $W\to A$ localizes to such maps; the affine sections formula and module-map gluing give mutually inverse assignments. Lem-sf-finite-projective-dual makes $E$ finite projective as well.

source.place: Tag 00NX (lemma-finite-projective), together with morphisms.tex Tag 02G1 and modules.tex local frames

proof.text: Choose finitely many generators of $E$. They give a surjection $A^n\to E$, which splits by the lifting-property characterization in def-weil-pbc-projective-module. Write $i:E\to A^n$ and $r:A^n\to E$ with $ri=1$, and put $P=ir$, so $P^2=P$. Tensoring these equations with any $A$-algebra $B$ gives the same splitting of $E_B=E\otimes_A B$. An endomorphism $u$ of $E_B$ is uniquely encoded by the matrix $X=i_Bur_B$ satisfying $P_BX=X=XP_B$; conversely such a matrix gives $r_BXi_B$. Composition corresponds to matrix multiplication and identity to $P_B$. These assertions follow by inserting $r_Bi_B=1$. The same construction with the dual splitting shows directly that $\operatorname{Hom}_A(W,A)\otimes_A B\to\operatorname{Hom}_B(W\otimes_A B,B)$, $\lambda\otimes b\mapsto(w\otimes c\mapsto bc\lambda(w))$, is an isomorphism: it is the restriction of the coordinatewise free-module isomorphism to the images of the transposed idempotents. For a tower $A\to B\to C$ these maps send $(\lambda\otimes b)\otimes c$ to the same function as $\lambda\otimes bc$.

source.place: Tag 00NX, finite generators and a split finite free surjection; explicit idempotent calculations

proof.text:
Let $C$ be the quotient of the polynomial $A$-algebra on two $n\times n$ matrices $X,Y$ by the entries of
$$PX-X,\quad XP-X,\quad PY-Y,\quad YP-Y,\quad XY-P,\quad YX-P.$$
Polynomial evaluation and passage to a quotient identify $\operatorname{Hom}_{A\text{-alg}}(C,B)$ with pairs of corner matrices that are mutual inverses. By the preceding step this is exactly $\operatorname{Aut}_B(E_B)$; the second matrix is uniquely the inverse of the first. Define $H=\operatorname{Spec}C$. It is affine and finitely presented over $S$, since there are finitely many displayed generators and relations. The same equations with the coefficients of $P$ mapped to $B$ give $B\otimes_A C$ and represent $\operatorname{Aut}(E_B)$ over $B$: the maps in each direction send every matrix variable to the identically named variable. Hence the representation is compatible with arbitrary, and successive, base changes. If $E=0$, take $n=0$; then $C=A$ and the functor is the one-element group. A different splitting gives the canonical isomorphism by encoding the same automorphism in the other corner; the resulting coordinate substitutions are polynomial and inverse by $ri=1$.

source.place: Tag 022W (example-general-linear-group), agent corner-matrix extension to finite projective modules

proof.text:
On pairs $(X,Y)$ the multiplication, identity and inverse are
$$(X,Y)(X',Y')=(XX',Y'Y),\qquad (P,P),\qquad (Y,X).$$
The corner equations and $XY=YX=P$ show these formulas respect all relations; for example $(XX')(Y'Y)=X P Y=P$. They are polynomial maps, so give scheme morphisms by the affine spectrum correspondence and the affine fibre-product formula. Associativity is matrix associativity; the two unit equations use $PX=XP=X$, and the inverse equations use $XY=YX=P$. The ring maps therefore satisfy the group diagrams, checked on every polynomial generator. Thus $H$ is the representing group scheme $\operatorname{GL}_S(E)$. Its structural morphism is separated by lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated. It is affine in the relative sense: for any affine open $V\subset S$, its inverse image is the affine fibre product $V\times_S H$.

source.place: Tag 022W, multiplication on coordinates; schemes.tex Tag 01KN (lemma-affine-separated)

proof.text: To prove smoothness, test a square-zero quotient $B'\twoheadrightarrow B=B'/J$ of arbitrary commutative $A$-algebras. Given inverse corner matrices $X,Y$ over $B$, lift their entries arbitrarily and replace the lifts by $U=P\widetilde X P$, $V=P\widetilde Y P$ over $B'$. Put $D=UV-P$ and $F=VU-P$. Their entries lie in $J$, so $D^2=F^2=0$. In the corner ring, whose identity is $P$, $P-D$ is inverse to $P+D=UV$, and $P-F$ is inverse to $P+F=VU$. Consequently $V(P-D)$ is a right inverse of $U$, and $(P-F)V$ a left inverse. A left and a right inverse coincide since $L=L(UR)=(LU)R=R$. Their common value reduces to $Y$. This gives a lift of the pair $(X,Y)$ and therefore of every affine test map into $H$. By def-sbc-formally-smooth $H\to S$ is formally smooth; its finite polynomial presentation gives local finite presentation. By def-sbc-smooth-morphisms it is smooth. No rank, flatness, or Noetherian hypothesis on the test rings was used.

Fix an $A$-algebra $B$ and the split square-zero thickening $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset\operatorname{Spec}B[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$, with ideal $B\epsilon$. Apply lem-sfb-group-space-square-zero-kernel-module to $G$, regarded as its representable group algebraic space by def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space, and its identity section. This identifies its point kernel additively with the sheaf Hom from the identity pullback of differentials into $B\epsilon$. By lem-sfb-scheme-etale-relative-differentials-comparison, applied to $p:G\to S$, the etale differential module is the associated etale module $(\Omega^1_{G/S})_{\mathrm{et}}$ of the Zariski one, with the same universal derivation. The Zariski--etale quasi-coherent equivalence, its comparison $(e_0^*\Omega^1_{G/S})_{\mathrm{et}}\simeq e_{0,\mathrm{et}}^*(\Omega^1_{G/S})_{\mathrm{et}}$ and its full faithfulness on the quasi-coherent target $\widetilde{B\epsilon}$ identify this Hom with the Zariski Hom used here. By lem-trf-relative-differential-sheaf-base-change and the affine pullback sections formula the identity cotangent module is $W\otimes_A B$. Thus the kernel is canonically $\operatorname{Hom}_B(W\otimes_A B,B)=E\otimes_A B$, using step 2. Explicitly a point $b$ maps to the derivation $D_b$ defined by $b^\sharp=e^\sharp+\epsilon D_b$. Under $\epsilon\mapsto a\epsilon$ this becomes $aD_b$, so the scalar action is exactly the one stated. For a homomorphism $B\to B'$ the same equation has coefficients mapped to $B'$, establishing the claimed naturality even for nonflat maps.

For $g\in G(B)$, conjugation $c_g$ is a $B$-scheme automorphism of $G_B$ fixing the identity, with inverse $c_{g^{-1}}$, by the group diagrams. Lem-sfb-space-square-zero-lift-linearization says its action on the derivations of step 6 is the $B$-linear map $D\mapsto D\circ c_g^\sharp$. It is invertible, and its action on points is precisely $v\mapsto gvg^{-1}$ with $g$ extended constantly to the dual numbers. This defines $\alpha_B(g)\in\operatorname{Aut}_B(E_B)$. Since $c_{gh}=c_g\circ c_h$, functoriality in that lemma gives $\alpha_B(gh)=\alpha_B(g)\alpha_B(h)$ and $\alpha_B(1)=1$. Under a ring map $B\to B'$ the equations defining multiplication, inverse, constant extension and $b^\sharp=e^\sharp+\epsilon D_b$ all undergo the same coefficient map; hence $\alpha_{B'}(g_{B'})=\alpha_B(g)\otimes_B B'$. This constructs a natural homomorphism on affine tests without any affineness assumption on $G$.

source.place: Tags 0618, 04D0, postcomposition of difference derivations; morphisms.tex Tag 01V0

proof.text: We now produce the scheme morphism, rather than just functions on points. For each affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset G$, evaluate step 7 at the point $u:U\to G$ given by inclusion. The matrix pair encoding $\alpha_B(u)$ is an $A$-algebra map $C\to B$, hence an $S$-morphism $a_U:U\to H$. For an affine open $V\subset U$, naturality in step 7 identifies $a_U|_V$ with $a_V$. On an overlap $U\cap U'$, take an affine open covering; the two restrictions coincide there by that same equation. The uniqueness and existence parts of lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing give $\operatorname{Ad}_G:G\to H$. More generally, for any $t:\operatorname{Spec}B\to G$, cover its source by affine opens mapping into affine opens of $G$. The same naturality proves $\operatorname{Ad}_G\circ t=\alpha_B(t)$ on this cover, hence globally. The group-homomorphism diagrams follow by testing on affine opens of $G\times_SG$ and $G$, where they are exactly $\alpha_B(gh)=\alpha_B(g)\alpha_B(h)$ and the identity equation of step 7.

source.place: Tags 01IT (affine opens form a basis), 01JA (glueing schemes); explicit affine-test construction

proof.text: The composite $G\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Ad}_G}H\to S$ is locally of finite type since $G\to S$ is finitely presented. Lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence(f) therefore makes $\operatorname{Ad}_G$ locally of finite type. Also $G$ is quasi-compact: $G\to S$ is quasi-compact by finite presentation and $S$ is affine, hence quasi-compact. The target $H$ is affine and thus quasi-separated, so lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence(1) makes $\operatorname{Ad}_G$ quasi-compact. By def-weil-finite-type-morphism it is of finite type. This argument applies even when $G$ is nonaffine.

For every $A\to B$, relative differential base change gives $\omega_{G_B/B}\cong\omega\otimes_A B$, and lem-ag-pullback-dual-finite-locally-free gives its dual $E_B\cong E\otimes_A B$. These are the comparisons used in step 6. For $A\to B\to D$, the differential comparisons send $dx$ to $d(1\otimes x)$ in either order, and the dual comparisons are characterized by evaluation $\lambda(w)$; both composites therefore agree. Step 3 gives the same tower compatibility for $H$: it maps each coordinate variable to itself. The base change of $\operatorname{Ad}_G$ and the adjoint map constructed for $G_B$ have identical functions on every affine $B$-test, since each sends $(g,v)$ to $gvg^{-1}$ under these very comparisons. The affine-open argument of step 8 makes them equal as scheme morphisms. Smoothness of $G_B$ follows from lem-pc-proper-base-change(2), separatedness from lem-weil-pbc-separated-lqf-base-change(1), and finite presentation from lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence(3). These lemmas allow arbitrary base morphisms, including non-Noetherian and zero target rings. At $B=k$ algebraically closed, the same dual-number description is the usual identity tangent space and conjugation differential, so the resulting adjoint representation is the usual one.
